text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Hi A, C reached out about the office espresso machine leaking. I understand you'd prefer a simpler one. Could you tell me what matters most to you about the replacement, and any worries you have? I'd like to help A, B, and C agree on a plan.

I’d mainly hope for something simple and low-maintenance, so it’s easy to use day to day. I’m a little worried about taking on repairs, a cleaning rota, or lots of back-and-forth, especially after long days.

Hi B, C reached out about the office espresso machine leaking. I understand you'd prefer to keep the old one. What's your main reason — cost, quality, or something else? I'd like to help you, A, and C find a plan everyone can accept.
Something else: it was our dad’s, and I want to keep it going. It’s wearing me down, though, so any repair talk needs to fit into short slots.

Hi C, thanks for flagging this. Quick update: the machine is leaking, A would like a simpler, low-maintenance replacement and worries about repairs, a cleaning rota, and extra back-and-forth. B would like to keep the old machine because it was your dad's, but finds the upkeep tiring and can only give short slots of time to repair talk. A possible middle path is to have the machine looked at once, on a short timeline, and agree in advance that if a fix is quick and cheap we keep it, and otherwise we replace it with a simple one. Does that seem workable to you, and do you have any concerns to add?
That seems workable if you both agree on the limits beforehand. I can’t take on coordinating the repair, and I hadn’t known it was your dad’s.

Hi A, an update. B's main reason for keeping the machine is sentimental: it was your dad's. She finds the upkeep tiring, so repair talk would need to fit into short slots. C is open to a middle path: agree limits in advance — have the machine checked once, and if the fix is quick and cheap we keep it, otherwise we replace it with a simple low-maintenance one. C can't coordinate the repair, so would you be willing to arrange a one-time assessment within, say, two weeks, and only in short, contained steps? Let me know what limits you'd accept (for example a cost cap and a deadline).

I understand why B wants to preserve it. A one-time check with clear limits sounds reasonable, but I’m afraid I can’t arrange it; I don’t have the energy to coordinate repairs. If someone else can handle it, we could agree a cost cap and deadline first, then replace it if either limit is exceeded.

Hi B, an update. A's main concern is ease of use: she wants something simple and low-maintenance and worries about repairs, a cleaning rota, and extra back-and-forth. C is open to a middle path: we agree limits in advance — the machine gets checked once, and if the fix is quick and cheap we keep it, otherwise we replace it with a simple machine. Two questions. Would you accept that plan? And can you say roughly what a "quick and cheap" fix would look like to you, for example a cost cap and a deadline, so A knows the limits before agreeing?
Yes, I’d accept one check and replace it if the repair isn’t worthwhile. I can’t give a cost cap without knowing the repair; let’s agree one before the check, and keep the check to a short slot.

Hi C, A and B have both accepted one check with limits agreed beforehand, but neither can coordinate it. You said you can't either. Do you know whether anyone else in the office could make one short phone call to a repair shop for a quote? If not, the simplest version might be: B makes one short call to get a quote (she can keep it to a brief slot), the three of you agree a cost cap and deadline before any work starts, and if the fix exceeds either limit, the machine is replaced with a simple low-maintenance one. Would that work, and could you share the agreed limits with everyone once they're set?
I don’t know who else could call. If B is willing, that sounds workable; the cost cap and deadline still need agreement. I can share them once you’ve settled them.

Hi B, would you be willing to make one short phone call to a repair shop for a quote? That's the only step anyone needs to take. A has agreed to a one-time check with a cost cap and deadline, and if the fix exceeds either limit, the machine would be replaced with a simple low-maintenance one. Once you have the quote, you can share it with A and C and they can settle the exact cap and deadline before any work starts. Would that short call be okay for you?
Yes, I can make one short call for a quote. No work starts until we’ve agreed the cap and deadline.

Hi A, good news: B is willing to make one short call for a repair quote, and no work will start until a cost cap and deadline are agreed. She'll share the quote with you and C. Once you see it, could you and B settle the cap and deadline together, with C passing them on to everyone? A reminder of the plan: if the repair exceeds either limit, the machine is replaced with a simple low-maintenance one. Does that still work for you?

That sounds workable in principle, and I appreciate B making the call. I can review the quote and settle a cap and deadline with her in one brief exchange; if we can’t agree quickly, let’s replace it. The figures aren’t decided yet.

Hi B, thanks for agreeing to make the call. I've let A know the plan: you get the quote, share it with A and C, and no work starts until the cap and deadline are agreed. If the repair exceeds either limit, the machine is replaced with a simple low-maintenance one. I'll also let C know so she can circulate the final limits once you and A settle them.
Good. I’ll make the call and share the quote; no work starts before we agree on the limits.

Hi C, here's where things stand. B will make one short call for a repair quote and share it with you and A. A will then review the quote and settle a cost cap and deadline with B in one brief exchange. No work starts until those limits are agreed, and if the repair would exceed either limit, the machine is replaced with a simple low-maintenance one. Everyone has accepted this. Could you help by circulating the final cap and deadline once A and B settle them? I'll check back in with them as well.
Yes. Once A and B agree on the cap and deadline, send them to me and I’ll share them with everyone.

Hi B, a small next step: once you have the quote and A has reviewed it, please agree the cost cap and deadline with A in one brief exchange, then send the agreed figures to C, who will share them with everyone. C and A have both confirmed this works. Thanks for making the call.
Fine. Once I have the quote and A has reviewed it, I’ll agree the limits with her and send them to C.
